metadata.title: Safe‑Halt vs Restore

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for determining when halting execution is safer than restoration or resumption.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Resilience decision-making, safe-halt mechanisms, recovery gating, and execution suppression.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Foundational Zero Trust pattern defining when safe halt is required instead of restore.

props.name: data-pattern
props.remarks: Defines safe-halt and restore eligibility as trust-relevant resilience decision data.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Continuity and recovery controls are constrained by safe-halt versus restore eligibility.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Zero Trust guidance requiring explicit authorization for resumption and continued operation.

metadata.remarks: Safe‑Halt vs Restore defines when cessation of execution is safer than system restoration or resumption. This pattern establishes non-equivalence between recoverability and safe operation.

components.title: Safe Halt Condition
components.description: Conditions under which execution must be halted to prevent further harm or unsafe outcomes.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Plans include explicit conditions requiring cessation of operation.

components.title: Restore Eligibility
components.description: Determines when system restoration would not introduce new risk or conceal harm.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Recovery is permitted only when restoration does not increase risk.

components.title: Halt as Default on Uncertainty
components.description: Defaults to halting execution when safety, correctness, or integrity cannot be conclusively established.

components.title: Halt vs Restore Non‑Equivalence Constraints
components.description: Explicitly defines what restoration capability does not grant or imply.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Ability to restore does not imply safety or permission to resume.

components.title: Safe Halt Signaling
components.description: Emission of halt-required signals to suppress restore, resume, or replay actions.
